sections.html:
The Randolph County Tax Department sets and bills property tax. Its website has separate pages for real property, rates, reappraisal, liens, the annual property tax scroll, relief applications and foreclosure sales, plus a tax bill lookup and a real property search.

Eleven municipalities appear on the county's rate page: Asheboro, Archdale, Franklinville, Liberty, Ramseur, Randleman, Seagrove, Staley, High Point, Thomasville and Trinity. Which charges reach your bill depends on whether the parcel lies in one of them and in which fire district.

The county rate listed for 2026-2027 is 0.50. City, school and fire rates are listed on top of it. Confirm the figures on your own bill with the tax department.

Two school rates are listed: 0.1153 for Asheboro and 0.0803 for Trinity. Eighteen fire districts carry rates from 0.10 for Staley to 0.18 for Climax.

  • Fire rates include Fair Grove 0.132, Guil-Rand 0.15, Julian 0.135, Westside 0.16, Eastside 0.17, Level Cross 0.17 and Ulah 0.12.
  • More fire rates: Seagrove 0.12, Tabernacle 0.1225, Northeast (Liberty) 0.17, Rand Soph 0.17, Coleridge-Erect 0.12, Franklinville 0.16, Bennett 0.11, Farmer 0.12 and Southwest (New Hope) 0.12.
  • Flat vehicle fees: High Point 30.00, Liberty 5.00 and Thomasville 20.00.
  • Dog fees: 5.00 in Randolph, 5.00 in Ramseur and 0.00 in Liberty.

A rural parcel pays the county rate plus a fire rate, and an in-town parcel adds its city rate. Ask the tax department to confirm your districts.

sections.h2: How the layers stack up for an Asheboro address
sections.html:
An in-town house in the Asheboro school area carries three layers: the county rate of 0.50, the Asheboro city rate of 0.71 and the Asheboro school rate of 0.1153. A fire rate can sit on top depending on the district, and the tax department can tell you whether yours does.

An address in Archdale, Franklinville or Seagrove draws on a different city figure, and a house outside every town skips the city layer entirely. That spread is why two Randolph County houses with the same assessed value can get different bills. When you list, tell a buyer which district you sit in, since the combined rate shapes the monthly payment on the buyer's loan.

Randolph revalues every four years, shorter than the state's eight-year minimum. The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2023, and the next is scheduled for 2027.

A proposed 2027 schedule of values and a proposed present-use schedule are posted, so treat them as drafts until commissioners act. The county aims for full market value on every parcel. A revaluation year is when many sellers see the biggest swing in assessed value, so read the notice when it arrives.

sections.h2: How the county values a house
sections.html:
Appraisers study sales in the county, record each property's size, construction, heating and cooling, plumbing, age and condition, and weigh the income a property could earn. Values do not move evenly. Depending on recent sales in a market area, an assessment may rise, fall or stay about the same.

A reappraisal sets only one half of the bill, the assessed value. Elected officials set the rate.

sections.h2: What the 2027 reappraisal means for a seller
sections.html:
It resets the assessed value that a buyer's first full bill is built on. Market value means the price both sides would accept without pressure. If your house is priced below what the county's appraisers see in nearby sales, expect a higher notice. If you have made repairs or additions, report them so the record matches.

  • Check your parcel in the county's real property search.
  • Read the reappraisal value notice as soon as it comes.
  • Use the informal appeal form mailed with the notice before moving to a board hearing.

sections.h2: Valid reasons to appeal in Randolph County
sections.html:
Randolph accepts two: an assessment far above market value, or one out of line with similar properties nearby. A value that simply feels too high, high taxes, or an owner who cannot afford the bill are not valid reasons.

The path runs through an informal appeal, mailed with each reappraisal notice, then Randolph's review board, the state commission that hears property tax cases and the appellate court. A commission appeal is due 30 days after the board mails its ruling (G.S. 105-290). Ask the tax department for the board's meeting dates.

sections.h2: Who is billed when a Randolph County house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever owned it on January 1. The bill is always generated for that owner. Randolph uses a permanent listing system, so land is listed automatically as soon as the register of deeds records a deed. Building changes still must be reported in the listing period.

You can pay the face amount through January 5. Interest of 2 percent starts January 6, with 0.75 percent per month from February 1 (the collection statute). Who shares which part of that year's bill is a closing negotiation.

sections.h2: Relief and collection rules for sellers
sections.html:
Randolph posts a relief page and an application form. The state programs are the senior and disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferment, and an owner can use only one. They sit in G.S. 105-277.1, G.S. 105-277.1C and G.S. 105-277.1B.

The circuit breaker defers the excess tax as a lien, and deferred tax for the three prior years comes due on a sale. If a bill stays unpaid, the county can foreclose through an action filed where the land lies, with a public auction at the courthouse door under G.S. 105-374. Selling first, even to a cash buyer, avoids that path.

The state listing period opens the first business day of January and closes January 31 (G.S. 105-307). Extensions are available for good cause but not past April 15. Land is listed on its own in Randolph, so the window matters for added rooms, removed structures and business equipment.

sections.h2: Checklist before listing a Randolph County house
sections.html:
A few quick checks keep the tax side from slowing the sale. Pull up your parcel in the real property search and confirm the record matches the house. Look up the tax bill online and write down any balance. Ask the tax department which city, school and fire rates apply. Find out whether a relief or deferral is attached. Then give all of it to your closing attorney.

If the house is inherited, vacant or needs work, a cash sale can close faster, but the tax payoff is still taken from your proceeds at the table.

faqs.q: What is Randolph County's reappraisal schedule?
faqs.a: A four-year cycle. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023, and the next is scheduled for 2027.

faqs.q: What county rate does Randolph County list for 2026-2027?
faqs.a: 0.50, with city, school and fire rates listed apart from it. Call the tax department to confirm your total.

faqs.q: Is high tax a valid reason to appeal a Randolph County value?
faqs.a: No. High taxes and an owner's inability to pay are not valid reasons. An appeal has to show the value exceeds market or is inconsistent with similar properties.

faqs.q: What is the Asheboro city rate?
faqs.a: 0.71, plus a school rate of 0.1153. Other towns carry different rates, so match the figure to your parcel.

faqs.q: Who receives the tax bill after a Randolph County sale?
faqs.a: The bill goes to the January 1 owner. How the buyer shares the cost is a closing matter.
